chunks: Aḥmad ibn Mihrān, may Allah have mercy on him, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from al-Ḥasan ibn Manṣūr, from his brother, who said:

I entered upon al-Riḍā عليه السلام in an inner room in the middle of the house at night. Then he raised his hand, and it was as though there were ten lamps in the house. A man then sought permission to enter upon him, so he lowered his hand, and then gave him permission.

key_terms.الرِّضَا: Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام, the central figure in the report
key_terms.بَيْتٍ: a room or house-space in which the event took place
key_terms.عَشَرَةَ: ten, used to describe the apparent number of lamps
key_terms.لَيْلًا: at night, indicating the darkness and setting of the event
key_terms.مَصَابِيحَ: lamps, expressing the intensity of the light seen in the room
key_terms.يَدَهُ: his hand, which is described as the source of the visible illumination

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith about Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام illuminating a room with his hand describe?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates an event from the life of Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام in which a radiant sign appeared when he raised his hand in a dark inner room. It highlights an extraordinary manifestation associated with the Imam عليه السلام and serves as part of the biographical reports that reflect his special station.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Mihran, from Muhamamd Bin Ali, from Al Hassan Bin Mansour, from his brother who said,

‘I went over to Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> in an inside room in the middle of the house one night, so he<sup>asws</sup> raised his<sup>asws</sup> hand, and it was as if there were ten lanterns in the house, and I sought permission for a man to see him<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> freed his<sup>asws</sup> hand, then permitted for him’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from those he mentioned from Safwan ibnyh who has said the following. “when abu Ibrahim (a.s.) passed away abu al-Hassan (al-Rida) (a.s.) spoke (about his Imamat) and we became afraid for him because of it. It was said to him, “You have declared a very great issue and we are afraid for you from this rebel.”
The Imam (a.s.) said, “Let him strive his best but he will find way against me.”
